items.stem: Compare the elongation phase and the meristematic phase on any three points.
items.answer: The elongation phase: zone just behind the meristem; new cell wall deposition; cell enlargement. The meristematic phase: thin cellulosic primary walls with many plasmodesmata; rich in protoplasm; large conspicuous nuclei.

items.stem:
Two leaves A and B were measured by Kunal in Dehradun. Leaf A grew from 5 cm² to 10 cm²; leaf B grew from 50 cm² to 55 cm² in the same day.
(i) Compare their absolute growth rates. (1 mark)
(ii) Calculate their relative growth rates. (2 marks)
(iii) Which leaf shows faster relative growth and why is this measure useful? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Both 5 cm² per day – equal. (ii) A: 5/5 = 1 (100%) per day; B: 5/50 = 0.1 (10%) per day. (iii) Leaf A; relative growth rate takes the initial size into account.

Which term describes an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ, its parts or even of an individual cell?
items.answer: growth

Gibberellin: Kurosawa – bakanae disease of rice by Gibberella fujikuroi; GA₃; effects – stem elongation, grape stalks, apple shape, delay senescence, malting, sugarcane yield, early seed production in conifers, bolting.

items.stem: Give two differences between cytokinin and auxin.
items.answer: Cytokinin: helps produce new leaves and chloroplasts; promotes cell division. Auxin: initiates rooting in stem cuttings; 2,4-D form used as a weedicide.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. cytokinin – helps produce new leaves and chloroplasts; promotes cell division; auxin – initiates rooting in stem cuttings; 2,4-D form used as a weedicide.

items.stem: Which term describes a condition in which a seed fails to germinate even under favourable external conditions because of internal (endogenous) factors?
items.answer: seed dormancy
items.markingKey: (a) Seed dormancy: a condition in which a seed fails to germinate even under favourable external conditions because of internal (endogenous) factors.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about plant growth regulators is correct?
items.answer: Ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants.
items.markingKey: (a) Ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants. The other statements are false. Cytokinins help overcome apical dominance; auxins promote it. ABA inhibits seed germination and induces dormancy. 2,4-D kills dicot weeds and does not affect mature monocot plants.
options: Ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants.
2,4-D is used to kill monocot weeds in wheat fields.

items.stem: A leaf grew from 5 cm² to 15 cm² in 5 days. What is its relative growth rate?
items.answer: 0.4 per day
items.markingKey: (d) Relative growth rate = growth per unit time / initial parameter = (15 − 5)/(5 × 5) = 0.4 per day.

items.stem: A plant in its exponential phase grows according to W₁ = W₀e^(rt). If the initial size W₀ = 10 g and the relative growth rate r = 0.1 per day, find the size after 4 days. (Take e as 2.718.)
Which of the following is a natural auxin?
items.answer: IAA (indole-3-acetic acid)
items.markingKey: (a) IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) is a natural auxin; the others are not.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Winter wheat must be exposed to low temperature to flower.
Reason (R): Vernalisation prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Cold exposure induces flowering in the next season.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “growth”?
items.answer: An irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ, its parts or even of an individual cell.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ, its parts or even of an individual cell.

items.stem:
A phase of plant growth is described: new cell wall deposition; increased vacuolation; zone just behind the meristem.
(i) Identify the phase. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the meristematic phase? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The elongation phase (ii) cell enlargement (iii) cells at the root and shoot apex divide constantly; rich in protoplasm
items.markingKey: (i) the elongation phase – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: cell enlargement – 1 mark. (iii) for the meristematic phase: cells at the root and shoot apex divide constantly; rich in protoplasm; large conspicuous nuclei – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: A plant growth regulator shows these effects: 2,4-D form used as a weedicide; initiates rooting in stem cuttings. Identify the PGR. Give a reason.
items.answer: Auxin
items.markingKey: 1 mark: auxin; 1 mark: the features 2,4-D form used as a weedicide; initiates rooting in stem cuttings are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as source of ethylene used in agriculture or natural auxin: IBA (indole butyric acid), IAA (indole-3-acetic acid), ethephon.
items.answer: IBA (indole butyric acid) – natural auxin; IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) – natural auxin; ethephon – source of ethylene used in agriculture.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: IBA (indole butyric acid) – natural auxin; IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) – natural auxin; ethephon – source of ethylene used in agriculture.

items.stem: Give two differences between a long day plant and a short day plant.
items.answer: A long day plant: short nights favour flowering; responds to photoperiod perceived in leaves. A short day plant: long uninterrupted dark period needed; responds to photoperiod perceived in leaves.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. a long day plant – short nights favour flowering; responds to photoperiod perceived in leaves; a short day plant – long uninterrupted dark period needed; responds to photoperiod perceived in leaves.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct phases of a sigmoid growth curve: stationary phase, log (exponential) phase, lag phase. Give a reason.
items.answer: lag phase → log (exponential) phase → stationary phase
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order lag phase → log (exponential) phase → stationary phase; 1 mark for the reason: Slow start, rapid growth, then a plateau as nutrients become limiting.

items.stem: Which of the following is a source of ethylene used in agriculture?
items.answer: ethephon
items.markingKey: (c) Ethephon is a source of ethylene used in agriculture; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The shoot apex perceives the photoperiod directly.”
items.answer: The leaves perceive the light/dark periods; a hormonal signal moves to the shoot apex.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The leaves perceive the light/dark periods; a hormonal signal moves to the shoot apex.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of oat coleoptiles.
Reason (R): Gibberellins were first isolated from human urine.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Auxins were first isolated from human urine; gibberellins were found from Gibberella fujikuroi.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “long day plants”?
items.answer: Plants that require exposure to light for a period exceeding a critical duration to induce flowering.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: plants that require exposure to light for a period exceeding a critical duration to induce flowering.

items.stem: Give two differences between the meristematic phase and the elongation phase.
items.answer: The meristematic phase: cells at the root and shoot apex divide constantly; large conspicuous nuclei. The elongation phase: increased vacuolation; cell enlargement.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the meristematic phase – cells at the root and shoot apex divide constantly; large conspicuous nuclei; the elongation phase – increased vacuolation; cell enlargement.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between cytokinin and gibberellin on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A plant growth regulator shows these effects: increases length of grape stalks. Identify the PGR – cytokinin or gibberellin? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Cytokinin: promotes cell division; helps produce new leaves and chloroplasts; overcomes apical dominance. Gibberellin: increases length of grape stalks; causes bolting in cabbage; speeds up malting in brewing. (b) Gibberellin.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: gibberellin; 1 mark: “increases length of grape stalks” is a feature of gibberellin.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as example of heterophylly in development or example of heterophylly due to the environment: buttercup, larkspur, coriander, cotton.
items.answer: buttercup – example of heterophylly due to the environment; larkspur – example of heterophylly in development; coriander – example of heterophylly in development; cotton – example of heterophylly in development.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: buttercup – example of heterophylly due to the environment; larkspur – example of heterophylly in development; coriander – example of heterophylly in development; cotton – example of heterophylly in development.

items.stem: Give two differences between cytokinin and abscisic acid.
items.answer: Cytokinin: promotes cell division; delays leaf senescence. Abscisic acid: inhibits seed germination; induces dormancy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. cytokinin – promotes cell division; delays leaf senescence; abscisic acid – inhibits seed germination; induces dormancy.

items.stem: Which term describes breaking an impermeable seed coat by mechanical abrasions or vigorous shaking to overcome dormancy?
items.answer: scarification
items.markingKey: (c) Scarification: breaking an impermeable seed coat by mechanical abrasions or vigorous shaking to overcome dormancy.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about plant growth regulators is correct?
items.answer: Gibberellins are used to increase the length of grape stalks and to elongate apples.
items.markingKey: (d) Gibberellins are used to increase the length of grape stalks and to elongate apples. The other statements are false. Cytokinins help overcome apical dominance; auxins promote it. Ethylene promotes ripening and enhances respiration rate during ripening (respiratory climacteric). Auxins were first isolated from human urine; gibberellins were found from Gibberella fujikuroi.
options: Gibberellins were first isolated from human urine.
Gibberellins are used to increase the length of grape stalks and to elongate apples.

items.stem: A leaf grew from 20 cm² to 60 cm² in 4 days. What is its absolute growth rate?
items.answer: 10 cm² per day
items.markingKey: (a) Absolute growth rate = increase per unit time = (60 − 20)/4 = 10 cm² per day.

items.stem: A plant in its exponential phase grows according to W₁ = W₀e^(rt). If the initial size W₀ = 2 g and the relative growth rate r = 0.2 per day, find the size after 4 days. (Take e as 2.718.)
